[RFCS.26.2] **The replayer applies the seeds before the first input.** A
replayer must apply each `CacheSeed` to the engine, in stream order, before the
replay's first stream event. It seeds `key` with the value `value_json` holds
and with the recorded deadline, as a host seed writes the cache
([IARC.12.1]): it raises no cache event and calls no write-through. The replay
clock follows the recorded clock values ([LFST.9.2.1]), so an entry expires
where it did in the run.

A seed the replayer applies is a host seed for [RFCS.26.1] and for [NLFC.9.3]:
a recording of the replay carries the same `CacheSeed` atoms, and the `initial`
block's cache item for the same key leaves it in place, as in the run. The integrator must not seed an
engine it replays into: the stream carries that engine's seeds, and one more
would start the replay from a cache the run did not have.

A recorded `CacheSeed` was stored when it was recorded. So an engine that
refuses one, as a cache bound the recording engine did not have refuses it
([LSTO.4.7.5]), and a `CacheSeed` after an event atom, which no recorder
writes, are a replay that has not reproduced the run. The replayer must stop
with `DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE`.
